Question
========

Betrachten Sie die folgenden Diagramme, die jeweils die Kovariation zweier nominaler Variablen darstellen. 

Welches Diagramm lässt am ehesten auf stochastische Unabhängigkeit schließen?

*Wählen Sie die passende Antwortoption!*

Hinweise:

- Orientieren Sie sich im Übrigen an den [allgemeinen Hinweisen des Datenwerks](https://datenwerk.netlify.app/hinweise).


```{r setup}
library(teachertools)
library(tidyverse)
data("teaching_data")
```





```{r prep-data}
all_vars_teaching_data <- 
  str_c(teaching_data$vars,collapse = ",") |> 
  str_split(pattern = ",") |> 
  unlist() |> 
  unique()

n_plots <- 4
all_vars_teaching_data_sample <-
  sample(all_vars_teaching_data, size = n_plots * 2)
```


```{r plot-association, out.width="70%", fig.width=15}
p1 <- teachertools::plot_nominal_association(mtcars, 
                         var1 = "mpg", 
                         var2 = "disp",
                         label1 = all_vars_teaching_data_sample[1],
                         label2 =  all_vars_teaching_data_sample[2])  # very strong

p2 <- teachertools::plot_nominal_association(
  mtcars, "qsec", "mpg",
  label1 =  all_vars_teaching_data_sample[3],
  label2 =  all_vars_teaching_data_sample[4])  # medium

data("Affairs", package = "AER")
p3 <- teachertools::plot_nominal_association(
  Affairs, "education", "rating",  #weak
  label1 =  all_vars_teaching_data_sample[5],
  label2 =  all_vars_teaching_data_sample[6]) 

p4 <- plot_nominal_association(Affairs, "religiousness", "rating",
                         label1 = all_vars_teaching_data_sample[7],
                         label2 = all_vars_teaching_data_sample[8])  # zero!

plots_list <- list(very_strong = p1, medium = p2, weak = p3, zero = p4)

plots_list <- sample(plots_list)
named_plots_list <- names(plots_list)

see::plots(plots_list, tags = "A", n_rows = 2)
```


```{r build-answer}
sol_df <-
  tibble(association = named_plots_list,
         correct_answer = ifelse(association == "zero", TRUE, FALSE),
         id = c("A", "B", "C", "D"),
         explanation = glue::glue("Strength of association: {association}"))
```



Wenn die Assoziation null ist, kann man von stochastischer Unabhängigkeit ausgehen.
Die Assoziation ist dann null, wenn die bedingten Häufigkeiten einer Variablen in Bezug auf die zweite Variable (annähernd) gleich sind.

```{r questionlist, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
answerlist(sol_df$id, markup = "markdown")
```

Solution
========

---

Aufgaben-ID: Abhaengige-Es

---



```{r sollist, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
answerlist(ifelse(sol_df$correct_answer, "Richtig", "Falsch"), sol_df$explanations, markup = "markdown")
```



```{r sol}
sol <- exams::mchoice2string(sol_df$correct_answer, single = TRUE)
```
